pymupdf4llm.snippet: We introduce syntactic modal operator ✷ **_⊢_** for _being a thesis_ into firstorder logic. This logic is a modern realization of R. Carnap’s old ideas on modality, as logical necessity (J. Symb. Logic, 1946) [1]. We place it within the modern framework of quantified modal logic with variable domains. We prove the completeness theorem using a property of a kind of normal form, and the fact that in the canonical frame, the relation on all maximal consistent sets, _R_ = _{⟨_ Γ _,_ ∆ _⟩_ : _∀A_ (✷ **_⊢_** _A ∈_ Γ = _⇒ A ∈_ ∆) _}_ , is a universal relation (both are unprovable in known quantified modal logics). The strength of the ✷ **_⊢_** operator is a proper extension of modal logic S5. Using completeness, we prove that satisfiability in a model of ✷ **_⊢_** _A_ under arbitrary valuation implies that _A_ is a thesis of formulated logic. So we can syntactically define logical entailment and consistency. Our semantics differ from S. Kripke’s standard one [3] in syntax, semantics, and interpretation of the necessity operator. We also have free variables, contrary to Kripke’s and Carnap’s approaches, but our notion of substitution is non-standard (variables inside modalities are not free). All ✷ **_⊢_** -free first-order theses are provable, as well as the Barcan formula and its converse. Our specific theses are ✷ **_⊢_** _A →∀xA_ , _¬_ ✷ **_⊢_** ( _x_ = _y_ ), _¬_ ✷ **_⊢_** _¬_ ( _x_ = _y_ ), _¬_ ✷ **_⊢_** _P_ ( _x_ ), _¬_ ✷ **_⊢_** _¬P_ ( _x_ ). We also have ✸ **_⊢_** _∃xA_ ( _x_ ) _→_ ✸ **_⊢_** _A_ (<sup>_y_</sup> _/x_ ), and _∀x_ ✷ **_⊢_** _A_ ( _x_ ) _→_ ✷ **_⊢_** _A_ (<sup>_y_</sup> _/x_ ), if _A_ is a ✷ **_⊢_** -free formula. **Key words** : R. the completeness of a variant of Carnap’s axiomatization, keeping Carnap’s original semantics almost untouched [2]. M. Madows formulated modern non-modal semantics for Carnap’s logic, together with a corresponding tableau system [5]. Madows interpreted logical necessity in a first-order structures as a quantification over all (parametrically definable) subsets of the domain of the structure. We believe that his approach can be considered a faithful modern representation of Carnap’s approach to logical necessity. Carnap’s necessity, as well as the necessities from the two cited works, actually does not express being a first-order thesis. For example, formulas like ✷ _A →∀xA_ , _¬_ ✷ _∃xy_ ( _x_ = _y_ ), and _¬_ ✷ _∃xy_ ( _x_ = _y_ ) should be provable if we were to think of ✷ as a logical necessity. As far as we know, there is no formalized version of Carnap’s ideas in the literature where logical necessity explicitly expresses being a first-order thesis. We aim to build a first-order modal logic with an operator expressing first-order theses and interpret it in a variant of variable domain semantics. For simplicity, we do not introduce function symbols and constants. To show that our modality ✷ **_⊢_** is factually correct, we prove that the satisfiability of any formula ✷ **_⊢_** _A_ in any model implies its logical validity and being a thesis, as we prove the completeness theorem.
